title: What Hinders Reintegration? A Qualitative Study on the Challenges Faced by Formerly Incarcerated Individuals in China
abstract: This study examines social reintegration challenges faced by formerly incarcerated individuals (FIIs) in China through 483 official case records, 13 in-depth interviews, and 2 months of fieldwork. Integrating rehabilitation and social integration theories, we identify four critical barriers, including institutional, economic, social, and psychological exclusion. Findings reveal a systemic disconnect between China’s resocialization policies and their implementation, creating a multi-layered exclusion mechanism. While some FIIs seek alternative belonging through mutual-aid communities or social enterprises, these mechanisms remain fragile without institutional support. The four-dimensional framework provides analytical tools for understanding reintegration barriers and offers implications for criminal justice policy refinement.
